name: RadioGroup
description: The APG radio group: one label over a set of radios, the arrow keys moving between them and choosing as they go. Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/

props.name: label
props.description: The group's name, rendered above it and used as the group's accessible name.

props.name: name
props.description: The `name` every radio in the group submits under. Generated when left out.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selection. Leave it out and the group owns it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The option chosen to begin with, when the group owns its value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires with the new value and why it changed — `'click'` or `'keyboard'`. A group can also hold nothing, so the value is `string | undefined`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which way the radios stack. Both arrow pairs navigate either way, as APG specifies.

props.name: children
props.description: The options: `RadioGroup.Item` elements, or anything else the group should hold.

parts.name: RadioGroup.Item
parts.description: A radio that reads its group: the shared `name`, whether it is selected, and what to report when it is chosen. Outside a `RadioGroup` it is a plain `RadioButton`.

props.name: value
props.description: What this radio submits, and what the group reports when it is chosen.

props.name: name
props.description: Only for an item rendered outside a group — inside one, the group supplies the name.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the radio, rendered inside a label that wraps the input.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Styles for the wrapping `<label>`: the row's layout, not the radio's own appearance.

props.name: props
props.description: Attributes for the `<input>` itself. `type`, `name` and `checked` are the group's.

props.name: ref
props.description: The `<input>` element, for a caller that has to focus or measure this option.

keyboard.action: Enters the group once, landing on the chosen option — or on the first, when none is chosen. Tab again leaves the group entirely.
The next option, choosing it as focus arrives, wrapping to the first.
The previous option, the same way, wrapping to the last.
Chooses the focused option. The platform supplies this one.

a11y: `role="radiogroup"`, named by its own `label` through `aria-labelledby` — radios with nothing over them are unrelated controls to a screen reader.
`aria-orientation` follows `orientation`, and every item shares one generated `name`, so the set submits as one field.
The tab order is deliberately the platform's: a native radio set is already one tab stop with a roving tabindex, which a `tabIndex` of ours would fight.
